subject: koala
pitch:
Category: Animal.
Subject: koala gripping a eucalyptus branch stand.
Style: pixel art.
reasoning:
I'm planning the design for a pixel art stand: a wooden base with a vertical eucalyptus branch post, and a koala clinging to the trunk facing forward.

I'll settle on the koala sitting upright, belly facing forward, with a horizontal branch at chest height to hug and another lower branch along X for its rump and legs to grip, flanked by a simple post-and-branch stand. Now I need to work out the actual dimensions for each piece.

Scaling the koala to roughly 0.65m sitting height within a 1.3m total model, I'm laying out the base as a wooden plank, with a tapered vertical trunk post offset to one side and a horizontal branch extending from it at chest height for the koala to grip.

I'm reconsidering the pose — maybe the koala should sit across a horizontal branch along X with a second parallel branch at chest height for its arms to grip, supported by two vertical posts forming a simple stand frame.

I'm working through the foot and hip placement so the koala's rump sits on branch A while the feet grip its front-bottom edge without overlapping the hip point, adjusting knee and foot coordinates to make the pose look natural.

I'll use a 3-point leg chain (hip, knee, ankle) with polyline segments for a faceted, blocky look rather than smooth catmull curves, then attach a foot box with toe boxes at the ankle. For the body, I'll loft/sweep over a spine chain running from hips through chest, neck, to head.

Now I'm laying out the spine points going from the hips up through chest, neck, to head, aiming for a pear-shaped body that's wide at the bottom and narrower at the chest, using a sweep with separate side and front-back radii. I'm sizing the koala's head big and round with proportionally huge fluffy ears and a prominent black spoon-shaped nose.

For construction style, I'm leaning toward blocky, pixel-art-inspired shapes: using boxy sweeps for the body and a Minecraft-style textured skin box for the head with a painted face, box ears with texture or stepped extrudes, and a dark pixel-highlighted nose block. I'm settling on a palette of grey fur tones, a lighter belly shade, white ear fluff, and black for the nose.

Now I'm working out proportions using a texel grid of 0.02 units, sizing the head box around 16x13x14 pixels to get realistic koala head width, with a separate snout box up front. For the skeleton I'm planning a root hips joint feeding into a spine chain, then neck, head, and a separate jaw box beneath the snout for the small koala mouth, plus ear joints branching off the head.

Then for limbs I'm figuring out finger joints per hand and foot — koalas have two opposable thumbs plus three fingers, so I'm budgeting around five digit joints per limb across four limbs, parenting each digit joint to the wrist or ankle and keeping the loop simple to stay within the overall joint budget.

Each digit becomes a two-joint chain shaped like a curled polyline so it wraps realistically around a branch, built with a small sweep for thickness, totaling roughly 40 joints across all digits which still leaves plenty of room under the 160-joint limit.

Now I'm figuring out the hand-to-branch positioning: placing wrists near the shoulders, bending the arm through an elbow, and resting the hand on top of branch B so the fingers can drape over its top and curl down the front face, computing per-digit x-offsets and the key wrist/finger coordinate points needed for that wrap.

Rather than hand-computing every mirrored side separately, I decide to use a side variable s (left = +1) to generalize the arm and finger coordinates across both sides using world-coordinate math.

Now I'm working out the leg joints: hip, knee, and ankle positions for each side so the koala's feet rest naturally on top of branch A, adjusting the squat angle so the knees come up and forward while the ankles tuck back toward the branch surface.

I need to check if the branch and body positions overlap in z-depth -- branch A at z=0 with body centered behind it means the feet planted at z=0 might clip into the body volume, so I'm adjusting the coordinates to keep the foot placement clear of the torso.

Working out leg joint positions: hips, knees, and ankles placed symmetrically on both sides outside the body width, with thighs angling forward-up and shins back-down for a squatting stance. Now I'm positioning the toes to wrap around branch A in the vertical plane, tracing a curve from the top of the branch down around its front and under its center.

Mapping toe digits spaced evenly along the x-axis with small pad radii, and planning matching hand digit spreads with darker grey coloring for the pads and fingers. I'm also figuring out where branch B sits -- horizontal along the x-axis at a higher position, with hands gripping it at specific x-offsets.

Now I'm checking how the chest front surface meets branch B's back surface, confirming contact. For the support structure, I'm settling on a single trunk off to one side with a forked branching pattern: a tall trunk with leaves at top, a rising cantilevered branch A extending across, and branch B as a curved path arcing forward using a smooth catmull-rom spline through several control points with varying radii.

Adding a second shorter post to help support branch A's far end, and planning leaf twigs at branch B's tip. For the eucalyptus leaves, I'm thinking of using textured double-sided quads with a small pixel-art leaf texture, placed as angled frames along the branches with a downward-hanging lean.

Placing leaf clusters at the trunk top and twig ends using a deterministic rng, skipping a twig near the koala's mouth since it's not holding anything. I'll use 2-3 green shades with a vein detail for the leaf texture, keeping the flat color palette small by relying mostly on cell painting rather than individual flat colors.

Now I'm setting the base material to white, then building a plank texture for the base using a tiled box approach — sizing the tile around 72x36 pixels so the top face shows roughly 65x35 texels, with horizontal plank rows every 6 pixels to create seam lines without randomness.

I'm positioning the base so its top sits at y=0.07 and the trunk sinks into it, keeping the model's lowest point at y=0. Then I'm defining color ramps for the fur (dark to light grays) and the belly cream tones for the pixel palette.

Setting up more color ramps for bark and leaves...

I'm checking texel density across the painted atlas—roughly 2.3mm per texel against 20mm cells gives about 9 texels per cell, which should stay crisp enough despite the pixelated magnification. Now I'm moving to the branch sweeps, planning bark texture with vertical streak patterns.

Skipping the peeling detail for now. For the head, I'm sizing the skin box using pixel dimensions scaled by the texel size, making the head proportionally larger than the shoulders in classic cartoon style, and giving the nose a big black oval shape centered slightly above the middle of the face using a finer texel scale.

I'll settle on body texel 0.02 and head texel 0.01, accepting the finer detail for small parts as intentional. Now I'm laying out the head sheet boxes: head [32,26,28], nose [8,8,5], and ears as small skin boxes around [12,12,3].

For the ears, I'm thinking a rounder fluffy shape sized about 0.2x0.19x0.06 with texel ~0.0125, using dark-grey rim pixels with a dithered white fluff center. I want transparent corner pixels to round off the box silhouette via alphaTest, leaving the box's side faces to carry the rest of the ear's texture layout.

Actually, a cleaner approach is building the ear as a stepped circular outline extrusion with cellPaint color at 0.05 thickness, then layering a smaller white extrusion in front for the fluff -- this keeps the pixel-art look through stepped geometry rather than texture cutouts. I'm working out the stepped circle rows now, with the ear spanning about 10 cells of 0.02 width.

I realize the fluff offset axis should instead derive from the cross product of the x and y directions, which flips sign with s to give (0,0,s) — keeping the thickness direction consistent regardless of mirroring.

I'll skip tilting the ears for simplicity and just position them at the sides of the head near the top, using the head's center and dimensions to set their x, y coordinates.

Working out the ear outline's origin point relative to its center, then shaping it as a rounded circle-like form with rows of varying half-widths to approximate curvature.

Fluff should sit slightly forward of the ear with a thinner protrusion, cream-colored with dither and dark edges, while the back of the ear stays dark fur. Then I'm moving to the head texture, drawing fur across all faces and placing small symmetric koala eyes with dark pupils and tiny highlights on the front face.

I'm adding lighter cream shading on the cheeks and chin, a lighter muzzle region around the nose, and a darker mouth line beneath it, while treating the jaw as a separate box positioned under the front of the head to form the lower face.

Setting up the spine chain curving from hips through chest to neck, then placing the head joint at the neck's end angled slightly forward so the head center sits above the shoulders.

Setting up a head joint, then sweeping a body along the spine chain with varying radii to get that pear-shaped pixel body—wide belly, narrower chest and top—considering whether box or octagon cross-sections give the chunkiest pixel-art look.

I'm deciding to mix sections, using boxes for limbs and an 8-sided ngon for the body, then adding round caps on the sweep so the hips get that rounded "sitting" base, calculating how far the dome extends past the path start to find the bottom y-coordinate.

Shifting hips to y=0.66 so the dome bottom lands at 0.49, which nestles neatly above branch A's top at 0.495. I'm reworking the spine, neck, head, and ear coordinates to match this new offset — head centered around 1.13 with its bottom at 1.0 and top at 1.26, ears sitting near y=1.24 flaring out at x=±0.17.

Now I'm working out arm placement, trying shoulder-elbow-wrist chains that let the hands rest on branch B around y=0.86-0.90. The bends keep coming out awkward, so I'm considering an alternative where the arms hug forward and down around the branch instead of reaching back.

Still placing finger wrap points and branch path coordinates...

Still plotting branch coordinates...

Writing leaf cluster generation logic...

Now I'm placing symmetric eye pixels with darker brow shadows above them and light highlight pixels for sheen, plus a dark mouth line near the jaw's bottom row and figuring out where the nose box should sit relative to the eyes.

Working out the nose's world coordinates and sinking depth, confirming it aligns with the pixel rows mapped to head geometry, then moving to figure out what texture sheet to use for the nose box.

For that, I'm sketching a small pixel pattern for a rounded nose with a dark ramp and a lighter highlight, then deciding to merge the head, nose, and jaw sheets into a single combined texture layout rather than separate textures.

Now I'm positioning the jaw box beneath the head's front face, aligning it so the mouth line sits at the bottom edge of the head and the jaw hinges forward from that joint, with a cream color darkening toward the lower edge and a tiny rounded chin accent.

I'm adding koala-style cheek fluff as small cream boxes at either side of the face, and planning ear placement centered near the top sides of the head with slight thickness along the depth axis, skipping eyebrows for now since the eyes are handled elsewhere on the texture sheet.

Still writing ear joint hierarchy...

Adjusting the ear fluff dimensions so it sits properly against the dark outer rim, with cream tufts layered along the edge for that fuzzy koala look.

Now I'm moving to the hands, planning a palm box geometry at the wrist and a helper function to generate finger digits as jointed chains along specified paths with per-finger offsets.

Writing finger chain code...

The arm chain's three points give the wrist tip, with the shoulder joint parented to the chest joint of the spine. For legs, I'm working out the hip positions relative to body width and leg radius to keep the parenting consistent.

Now I'm figuring out the leg and foot placement -- knee and ankle coordinates, then the toe path curving from ankle down toward the branch surface, checking the foot points stay consistent with the branch's top radius and front surface offset.

For construction, I'm skipping fancy limb IK and complex fur tufts for simplicity, but adding small bark knots and nubs scattered on the branches, a hanging eucalyptus gum nut capsule or two, and maybe some moss for extra detail on the stand.
